concept: Career Launch, First 90 Days And Field Habits
title: Career Launch, First 90 Days And Field Habits Checkpoint

questions.prompt: Which first-30-days plan is concrete and realistic?

options.label: Run the stack, map owners, shadow a deployment and reproduce a known issue.
Promise unrestricted customer access on day one.
Rewrite the platform before learning its operational constraints.

questions.explanation: Learning and a bounded reproduction create useful evidence early. Access and major redesign depend on context and authorization.

questions.prompt: How should you assess travel and on-call expectations for a role?

options.label: Assume every FDE job matches one public posting.
Infer support hours from the company's logo.
Verify the current arrangements with the hiring team and concrete deployment examples.

questions.explanation: Role expectations vary by team and location. A title, isolated posting or brand cannot establish the actual working agreement.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a public application portfolio?

options.label: A production credential to make review convenient.
Work you are authorized to share, with synthetic replacements for private material.
An employer's private customer dataset because you worked on it.

questions.explanation: Participation in a project does not grant disclosure rights. Show credible original evidence without exposing customer data or credentials.

questions.prompt: After the path, what is the most useful next learning decision?

options.label: Choose a demonstrated technical gap and a customer-facing gap for focused practice.
Repeat only the easiest quizzes to preserve a perfect score.
Collect more tool names without building or explaining anything.

questions.explanation: Targeted practice improves weak capabilities. Score maintenance and vocabulary collection provide little evidence of transferable delivery skill.
